name: Tencha

processing.description: Same covers as gyokuro. The leaf is destined for flakes, not needles.
蒸青, then destemmed and deveined. That missing 揉捻 is why tencha is not gyokuro.
Unrolled leaf. Most of it is milled to matcha. If you brew the flakes, treat them like gyokuro — not as a second timer mode.

taste: umami, lighter than matcha because you do not drink the powder
profile.mouthfeel: soft infusion if brewed, or none if milled

gongfu.curveException: Japanese greens go long–short–long: the first cool steep needs time, the second is quick because the leaf is open, the third lengthens again.

coldBrew.notes: 氷出し / kōridashi — ice on the leaf, melt, no kettle. A canonical Japanese cold brew, not a leftover trick.

water.note: Soft, cool. Treat like gyokuro if brewing the flakes.

storage: Freezer. Tencha is matcha’s perishable parent.

shelfLife.note: Warm the sealed packet to room temperature before opening.

commonFaults.name: stale tencha milled into dull matcha

summary: Unmilled shaded leaf: the raw material of matcha, occasionally brewed as flakes.
